content.text:
We need to assign orders to the four occupied regions: pyke, ironmans-bay, port-of-pyke, greywater-watch. Need to respect starred order limit: current King’s Court track shows order star availability per house. Tracks: kingsCourt ["lannister","stark","martell","baratheon","tyrell","greyjoy"] – position of Greyjoy is 6th (last). Need to see stars at position 6. In 6-player game, stars per position: I recall typical King’s Court track has stars: position1 = 3, 2=2, 3=2, 4=1,5=1,6=0? Actually need exact values. In base game, King’s Court track: position 1: 3 stars, 2: 2 stars, 3: 2 stars, 4: 1 star, 5: 1 star, 6: 0 stars. So Greyjoy at position6 has 0 stars, meaning cannot use any starred orders. So starred_preference avoid is default. We must assign order type for each region.

We have 4 regular orders (10 total available, but we need assign one per region). Types: March, Defense, Support, Consolidate Power, Raid. Need to decide best plan to gain castle areas: from pyke can march to Flint's Finger (castle) or Seagard (castle). From greywater-watch can also march to Flint's Finger, Moat Cailin (castle), Seagard (castle). Also we have a ship at ironmans-bay (a ship). Ironman's Bay is sea area with our ship. There is no unit in port-of-pyke (a ship). Port-of-pyke has a ship. We could use a March order from port-of-pyke (a ship) to move ships? March order could move ship further, but ships don't capture castles directly; they must transport land units. Could use support to aid other battles, but currently no nearby combats expected. Consolidate power would give power token in sea area which yields none, so probably waste. Raid could disrupt opponent's orders likely limited.

Goal: attempt to capture a new castle. Could assign March order with +0 (regular March) from pyke to Flint's Finger (adjacent?) Need adjacency: pyke neighbors? From map, pyke is land with sea neighbor ironmans-bay via ironmans-bay sea? Actually pyke connects to ironmans-bay (sea) and port-of-pyke (port). To march land units from pyke to Flint's Finger, need ship transport because they are not adjacent directly? Let's examine neighbours: pyke [land] neighbours: ironmans-bay (sea), port-of-pyke (port). Flint's Finger is land area connected to bay-of-ice, greywater-watch, ironmans-bay, sunset-sea. Pyke is not directly adjacent to Flint's Finger. However ship transport: if we have ship units in ironmans-bay, they can transport land units from pyke to Flint's Finger if there is a chain of sea areas with ships connecting. The rules: land units can be moved via ship transport across successive sea areas with ships, treating as adjacent. So from pyke (land) with footman/knight, need a ship in adjacent sea area (ironmans-bay). Then can march to any land area adjacent to ironmans-bay that has ship? Actually ship transport: land units can move from a land area to another land area if there is a chain of sea areas each containing at least one friendly ship, connecting the two coastal land areas. So we could march from pyke (land) to Flint's Finger (land) via ironmans-bay (sea) which contains a Greyjoy ship. Flint's Finger is adjacent to ironmans-bay (yes, from map: flints-finger [land] neighbours ironmans-bay). So ship transport works: pyke -> ironmans-bay (sea) -> flints-finger. Thus a March order from pyke can move footman/knight to Flint's Finger capturing castle.

We have footman and knight at pyke. Good. So assign March order to pyke, likely with +0 modifier (March +0) unless we want +1 but need special March +1 star, not available. So March +0.

Port-of-pyke contains a ship. Could march that ship somewhere else, but ships cannot move via March? Actually March order can be placed on a sea area or port? Order token must be placed on area with units (including ship) to move them. A March order on a port would move ships into adjacent sea area (or vice versa). Could use to move ship from port-of-pyke to ironmans-bay? But port-of-pyke is connected to pyke (land) and ironmans-bay (sea). The ship in port-of-pyke could be marched into ironmans-bay (sea) or into pyke (land) but cannot march into land unless it's a ship? Actually ships cannot march into land areas; they can only move in sea/port. So March order on port-of-pyke could move ship into ironmans-bay (sea) or other sea? Probably allowed. But we might want to reposition ship to support further moves later. Maybe we want to move ship from port-of-pyke to ironmans-bay (sea) to combine with ship already there, making a fleet for transport.

Alternatively, we could use Support order on greywater-watch to support pyke's march? Support orders can be placed in adjacent area to combat. But we aren't expecting combat. So maybe we can set Raid orders to disrupt opponent. But not urgent.

Greywater-watch has footman. Could assign March order from there to Moat Cailin (castle stronghold?) Moat Cailin is a castle area with castle=1. Yes Moat Cailin has castle=1. It's adjacent to greywater-watch directly? Yes map: greywater-watch neighbours moat-cailin. So we could march footman from greywater-watch to Moat Cailin capturing it (if unoccupied). That's good.

But note: we need to preserve supply: currently supply=2, we have two units in pyke (footman+knight) forming an army of size2 (counts as 1 army of size2). In greywater-watch we have footman alone (single unit not army). In ironmans-bay we have ship alone (single). In port-of-pyke ship alone (single). Supply limit of 2 allows armies: supply 2 permits army sizes: 3,2,2 (from table). So we can have up to three armies, largest size 3. Currently we have one army (pyke size2) and two single units (ships) not counted. So within limits.

If we move footman from greywater-watch to Moat Cailin via March, that would create an army of size1? Actually moving single unit to Moat Cailin will be a single unit there (still not army). That's fine.

If we move the footman/knight from pyke to Flint's Finger, they'd become single units in separate areas unless they both move together. March order can move any number of units from the area with order. They could both move together to the same destination (Flint's Finger) making an army size2 there. That will still be supply okay.

We need to consider that after marching, pyke becomes empty (no units). If we vacate pyke, we need to consider control: Home area pyke is home, so control remains without power token. So safe.

Thus orders: pyke: March. greywater-watch: March (to Moat Cailin). Ironmans-bay: maybe Consolidate Power? But in sea area, Consolidate Power gives power token based on power icon (none) and plus 1. There are no power icons, so not useful. Could do Raid to disrupt opponent support near? Adjacent areas: ironmans-bay adjacent to flints-finger, greywater-watch, port-of-pyke, pyke, seagard, sunset-sea, the-golden-sound. Opponent orders? unknown. Might be waste.

Port-of-pyke: could do Consolidate Power (sea) which gives 1 power token (order token) - actually gives one power token plus power icons (none). So Consolidate Power yields 1 power token (since base token). That would increase power tokens from 6 to 7, beneficial. So assign Consolidate Power to port-of-pyke. That's allowed: Consolidate Power in sea area yields power token (still counts). Yes.

Thus assignments:

pyke: march, avoid (no stars), priority high (maybe 90).
greywater-watch: march, priority maybe 80.
port-of-pyke: consolidate_power, priority 70.
ironmans-bay: defend? Or raid? Could also consolidate power but yields same as port - but we have only one consolidate power token? We have two regular Consolidate Power tokens (orderLegend 10,11) and one starred (12). No limit on using both, as we have 2. So we could use Consolidate Power on ironmans-bay also. But need to allocate orders for each region; we can assign consolidate_power to both sea areas to gain 2 power tokens. That's good.

But we must respect number of Consolidate Power tokens: we have 2 regular, 1 starred. Starred not allowed (no stars). So we have two regular, we have two sea areas, perfect. So assign Consolidate Power to ironmans-bay and port-of-pyke.

Thus orders:

pyke: march
greywater-watch: march
ironmans-bay: consolidate_power
port-of-pyke: consolidate_power

All starred_preference "avoid". Priorities maybe 100 for pyke, 90 for greywater-watch, 80 for ironmans-bay, 70 for port-of-pyke. Must be integers 0-100.

Let's craft JSON accordingly.

actionOutputSchema.description: You are placing planning orders for this round. Assign an order preference to each required occupied area, respecting the displayed restrictions and starred-order limit. Your final answer submits the whole order draft and marks your house ready. These orders determine what your armies can do later; this decision does not move units. A single land unit can capture an empty castle with a March order. Defence and Support orders do not move that unit or claim neighbouring land. Consolidate Power in an open sea earns no power; a port follows the separate port rule. The harness allocates the physical order tokens, preserving higher-priority preferences when not all requested categories fit the available tokens. Priority 100 is most important; 0 is least important. Plan how to gain castle areas this round. Use Defence or Support when you have a concrete battle to protect or assist; otherwise these orders can leave an army unable to expand.
